correctness.rationale: For the generalized Sprott O vector field, direct differentiation gives the exact coboundary \(L(xy+z-bx)=x^2+y^2+ax\). Every compact invariant probability therefore satisfies \(\mathbb E[(x+a/2)^2+y^2]=a^2/4\). Stationarity of \(x\) and \(y\) gives \(\mathbb E[y]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[x]=\mathbb E[z]=m\), yielding the variance parabola. Zero variance at either endpoint forces the corresponding equilibrium atom, using the displayed \(L(yz)\) identity. On the boundary circle, \(LF=y(4x-2z+a)\); if a complete trajectory is not an equilibrium, an interval with \(y\ne0\) forces a linear relation between \(z\) and \(x\), and substitution back yields a nonzero quartic vanishing on an interval, a contradiction. Hence only equilibrium mixtures live on the circle, and every other invariant measure has positive mass on both sides. Periodic-orbit crossing follows by continuity. The exact sparse-polynomial verifier checks all algebraic identities.
residual_risks: The measure theorem assumes compact support and does not address unbounded orbits.

value.rationale: The stationary circle is a parameter-exact geometric constraint on every compact recurrent statistical state of a standard generalized chaotic flow. The theorem also classifies the boundary-supported invariant measures and forces every nonconstant periodic orbit to cross the circle, turning a simple coboundary into a global recurrence statement. This is a natural structural property of the named flow rather than a numerical curiosity.
residual_risks: The result does not prove existence of a chaotic attractor in any parameter regime.
